\NLFrontMatterSection{Executive summary}

This document provides one traceable trade-off matrix row for each of the 2,088 unique requirements and components covered by the risk register. Every row identifies the decision focus, applicable alternative set, six-criterion score vector, weighted result for three alternatives, preferred preliminary disposition, and the condition that can change the decision.

Requirements remain mandatory. A trade study selects a compliant realization; it cannot vote away a shall-clause, human-authority boundary, independent QA obligation, commissioned-TPS role, DICOM/DICOM-RT validation, risk control, or release condition. A noncompliant alternative is infeasible regardless of score.

\begin{nlnotice}{PRELIMINARY DECISION STATUS}
Scores are structured prompts for engineering and clinical discussion, not validated measurements or automatic decisions. Project-specific evidence shall replace the preliminary scores. The decision record shall document alternatives, criteria, weights, assumptions, uncertainty, sensitivity, conflicts, risk effects, recommendation, decision authority, and implementation conditions.
\end{nlnotice}

\section{Decision-analysis method}

The matrices use weighted multi-criteria decision analysis. Each criterion is scored from 1 (least favorable) to 5 (most favorable). Weighted total is the sum of score multiplied by criterion weight, divided by 100. Ties or differences below an institution-defined meaningful threshold require sensitivity analysis rather than automatic selection.

\section{Alternative sets}

\begin{scriptsize}
\begin{longtable}{@{}L{0.07\textwidth}L{0.275\textwidth}L{0.285\textwidth}L{0.29\textwidth}@{}}
\toprule
\rowcolor{NLTableHeader}\textbf{Set} & \textbf{Alternative A} & \textbf{Alternative B} & \textbf{Alternative C} \\
\midrule
\endfirsthead
\toprule
\rowcolor{NLTableHeader}\textbf{Set} & \textbf{Alternative A} & \textbf{Alternative B} & \textbf{Alternative C} \\
\midrule
\endhead
\midrule
\multicolumn{4}{r}{\scriptsize Continued on next page} \\
\endfoot
\bottomrule
\endlastfoot
R & Primarily procedural or shared-service compliant realization with checklist, explicit human control, and retained records. & Bounded deterministic workflow or service with versioned policy, human gate, audit, monitoring, and verification. & Independent or redundant validator/control with isolation, diverse check where justified, automated reconciliation, and containment. \\
\addlinespace[2pt]
I & Endpoint-local contract and validation with controlled manual reconciliation and route-specific commissioning. & Shared versioned contract, trusted gateway, deterministic validation, atomic transaction control, explicit outcome, and reconciliation. & Independent producer and consumer validation plus shadow or dual comparison, automated quarantine and reconciliation, and enhanced continuity. \\
\addlinespace[2pt]
C & Consolidate the logical responsibility into an adjacent service or team under an explicit internal contract and evidence boundary. & Maintain a distinct logical component responsibility with stable contract, owner, configuration, monitoring, failure behavior, and independent test boundary. & Deploy isolated or redundant instances/control planes with independent validation, recovery, and enhanced separation of duties. \\
\addlinespace[2pt]
O & Controlled manual procedure and records with trained roles, checklist, escalation, and periodic review. & Governed workflow tooling with accountable approvals, controlled automation, audit, monitoring, and exercise evidence. & Independent automated enforcement plus secondary oversight, resilience, continuous monitoring, and tested continuity. \\
\addlinespace[2pt]
\end{longtable}
\end{scriptsize}

All alternatives are conditional on full compliance. Alternative A is infeasible when a deterministic, automated, independent, real-time, or commissioned control is explicitly required. Alternative C is not inherently safer if it adds common-cause software, latency, alert burden, inconsistent states, new attack surface, or operational complexity.

\section{Decision gate and required trade-study record}

Before implementation or release, each material decision shall identify the decision authority, alternatives considered, compliance screen, evidence sources, criterion definitions, weights, scores, uncertainty ranges, sensitivity to weights and assumptions, risk-control effects, cybersecurity and human-factors effects, common-cause and dependency risks, cost and schedule basis, dissent, final selection, conditions, monitoring, and change triggers.

A preferred C disposition does not automatically require a second full system. The team shall identify the minimum independence or diversity needed to reduce the specific hazard without introducing inconsistent state, latency, alert burden, new attack surface, or unmanageable support complexity. A preferred B plus targeted C disposition means baseline componentization with independent safeguards only at the risk-significant decision or data boundary.
